title: Generic point ideal inclusion filtration step

proof.text: Construct J=vanishingIdeal T and Z=J.subscheme. The source-library reduced subscheme instance and closed embedding identify Z with the irreducible closed subset T, giving IsIntegral Z. Its generic point maps to xi by genericPoint_spec.image and uniqueness of generic points in the T0 space X.

Rewrite the maximal-ideal annihilation hypothesis along the equality i(genericPoint Z)=xi. Apply coherent_generic_point_ideal_inclusion to get r,I,alpha and an open neighbourhood W on which alpha is invertible. The equality Supp(F)=T and the generic-point membership show that the target stalk there is nonzero.

Apply coherent_ideal_sum_cokernel_reduction to obtain I nonzero, coherent source A, coherent Q=cokernel alpha, and Supp(Q) strictly contained in Supp(F)=T. Apply hsmaller to Q. Apply coherentIntegralFiltration_ideal_sum to A.
Mono alpha and ShortComplex.exact_cokernel alpha give the canonical short exact sequence A -> F -> Q. Apply coherentIntegralFiltration_of_shortExact to the two filtrations.

theorem coherentIntegralFiltration_generic_step
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (T : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X) (ξ : X)
    (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ (T : Set X))
    (hsmaller : ∀ (G : X.Modules), RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G →
      {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (G.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊂ (T : Set X) →
      HasCoherentIntegralFiltration G)
    (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F)
    (hSupp : {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} = (T : Set X))
    (hkill : ∀ a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk ξ),
      ∀ m : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace ξ).obj F, a • m = 0) :
    HasCoherentIntegralFiltration F
